{"id":"PKIX-8d92","title":"pkix-path: ~45 survivors left, led by the name-constraint intersection","description":"## Why

pkix-path's sweep found 100 survivors; roughly 45 remain after five rounds
of fixes. Grouped by what they are about.

## Clusters

**Name-constraint intersection in chain_walk.** The `subtree_within` calls
and `already_in_result`. This is RFC 5280 §6.1.4 (g) permitted/excluded
subtree intersection -- the machinery that makes a constraint on an
intermediate bind everything below it. Highest value of what is left:
a wrong intersection is a trust-scope defect, which is the class the
§4.2.1.10 and SMTP-DANE findings earlier in this sweep belonged to.

**§6.1.1 path length.** `>` to `>=` on the max-path-length comparison, and
the `max_chain_certs` arithmetic. Boundary cases, the same shape as the CRL
and OCSP freshness windows closed in pkix-revocation: inclusive at the
documented end, and nothing asserts which end.

**policy_graph (3).** RFC 5280 §6.1.3/§6.1.4 policy mapping and the
valid-policy tree.

**sha1_digest (3).** Verify-only, opt-in per the project stance. Pinning it
needs a known-answer vector, which is a two-line test against the RFC 3174
sample.

**serde_der.rs (11).** The DER serde shims. Same class as
pkix-revocation's `crl_reason_serde`, where a round-trip over every variant
with hand-written wire values killed all eleven -- that is the template.

**check_max_validity.** One comparison.

**NormalizedIter / DirStringBytes (5).** RFC 4518 string prep internals
feeding `names_match`. Behavioural, and `names_match` is security-relevant;
these want direct unit tests on the iterator rather than tests through DN
comparison.

**Public helpers with no in-crate caller.** `cert_is_ca`,
`tbs_certificate_der`. A crate-scoped sweep cannot reach them by
construction; consumers may cover them, and that needs checking per case
rather than assuming either way. `pkix-identity`'s
`dns_name_matches_pattern` was the same shape and did turn out to be
entirely untested.

## Method

Re-run to regenerate the list:

    cargo mutants -p pkix-path --all-features -j 4 --timeout-multiplier 4

Six mutants timed out on the first run; `--timeout-multiplier 4` is what
keeps a slow-but-correct test from being read as a hang.

{"notes":"## Fresh sweep, 2026-11-27

    556 mutants, 47 missed, 439 caught, 64 unviable, 6 timeouts

Down from 100 missed. The 6 timeouts are `DirStringBytes::next` and
`NormalizedIter::next` -- the RFC 4518 string-prep iterators. A timeout
means the mutation makes the suite hang rather than answer wrongly, so
those are detected; they are not coverage gaps.

Closed since: NcTypeMask's eight constraint bits and both union operators
(417509f1), the unevaluable-name-form rules in check_san_name_form and the
emailAddress guard in check_name_constraints (15eb83c8), and the option /
vec / option_vec serde helpers (ac430b2b).

## What is left, by cluster

**chain_walk, 6.** The name-constraint intersection. 4192/4193 and 4218 are
the two-way `subtree_within` dedup conjunctions, 4195 the
`!already_in_result`, and 3934/3959 two `==` comparisons. 4218 is the
fail-open one: it dedups EXCLUDED subtrees, and a one-way containment
treated as equality drops the broader exclusion, so names that should be
excluded are allowed. Wants a chain where two CAs exclude nested subtrees
(`sub.bad.example` then `bad.example`) and a leaf under the broader one.

**The RSA-PSS backend, ~10.** verify_rsa_pss (3), rsa_public_key (2),
pad_prehash (2), rfc4055_hash (1), and three `verify_signature -> Ok(())`
at lib.rs:781 and :811. The Ok(()) ones are the fail-open shape -- a
verifier that accepts everything. Known-answer vectors are the cheap way
in: RFC 4055 and the NIST PSS test vectors.

**validate_path / max_chain_certs, 4.** `>` to `>=` at 1680 and 1694, and
the arithmetic at 1822. Boundary cases, the shape already closed for the
CRL and OCSP freshness windows in pkix-revocation: assert the documented
end is inclusive.

**policy_graph, 3.** intersect_user_policy_set, apply_policy_mappings,
prune_above_deepest -> (). RFC 5280 §6.1.3/§6.1.4.

**Public helpers with no in-crate caller, 5.** cert_is_ca (2) and
tbs_certificate_der (3). A crate-scoped sweep cannot reach them by
construction; consumers may cover them, which needs checking per case.
pkix-identity's dns_name_matches_pattern was this shape and was entirely
untested.

**Display / source / eq / hash, 6.** lib.rs:230 `eq -> true`, :255 `hash`,
:307 and :571 `fmt -> Ok(())`, :313 and :650 `source -> None`. The pattern
is settled: enumerate the variants, assert non-empty and pairwise
distinct, the way pkix-revocation's display_tests does. `eq -> true` is the
one with teeth -- it is a trust-anchor or DN equality.

**ip_constraint_within, 1.** `==` to `!=` at 3152.

**NcTypeMask::RFC822's shift, 1.** `1 << 0` and `1 >> 0` are the same
number. Unkillable; noted in the module."}

{"notes":"## Closed, 2026-11-27 (evening)

All nine verifiers.rs survivors and all nine lib.rs survivors are closed,
every mutation hand-verified (apply, run, confirm the test fails,
restore). Commits 8751cf20, 939bdeed, 7cf324d3, b2f735b8, 1e7ee684.

### verifiers.rs, 9

Two were equivalent and are gone with the code. `pad_prehash` left-padded
an ECDSA digest to the field width because `ecdsa` 0.16's `bits2field`
refused a prehash shorter than half the field size. `ecdsa` 0.17 converts
with `bytes2scalar`, which truncates a wide digest and reduces a narrow
one as it stands -- SEC 1 v2 4.1.4 step 5 directly -- so the function
returned its own argument for every curve-and-digest pair this crate
assembles. Removed; the comments at both prehash sites now name what the
dependency does, so a version that reintroduces a minimum length fails
sigalgs and legacy_sha1 instead of passing silently.

The other seven are parameter rules, each fail-open when loosened:

  RFC 3279 2.3.1   an rsaEncryption key's parameters MUST be NULL
  RFC 4055 1.2     an id-RSASSA-PSS key is restricted to PSS
  RFC 4055 2.1     the SHA-384 row of the hash table (sigalgs has PSS
                   with SHA-256 and SHA-512 and nothing between)
  RFC 4055 3.1     one hash for the digest and MGF1; a key's own
                   parameters pin the hash and floor the salt length
  RFC 8410 3       id-Ed25519 takes absent parameters

A certificate cannot express any of these: its signatureAlgorithm is
covered by its own signature, so altering a parameter to disagree with
the signature also invalidates it, and the disagreement is the subject.
So tests/fixtures/alg-params/ holds the four arguments of
verify_signature as raw DER -- one RSA modulus and one Ed25519 key
wrapped several ways, with signatures genuine for the parameters they are
named after. tests/alg_params.rs, nine tests.

### lib.rs, 9

- Display/source/eq/hash on Error and DerError (6). No in-crate caller,
  and each fails quietly in its own way: a Display that writes nothing
  still returns Ok, a source that answers None still satisfies the trait,
  an eq that answers true makes two DER failures one value, and since
  Error derives PartialEq a test asserting a particular Error::Der would
  then pass for the wrong one. All 23 variants render distinctly, with
  the chain index held constant so the assertion is about the messages.
- ip_constraint_within's `== 32` arm (1). Only the 8-byte arm was
  reached. The function answers bool, so a build that could not read an
  IPv6 constraint reports "not contained" rather than "could not tell".
  Both families now have a containment relation and its converse, and
  five non-constraint lengths are refused by name -- a 16-byte value is a
  bare IPv6 address, and read as a constraint its second half becomes
  the mask, so two all-zero blobs would contain each other.
- check_max_validity's `>` (1). Every existing test sat orders of
  magnitude from the cap, so `>=` left them all passing while refusing a
  certificate whose validity is exactly the configured cap. Both bounds
  now come from the fixture's own validity period.
- NcTypeMask::RFC822's `1 << 0` (1). Equivalent: `1 >> 0` is also 1.
  Recorded in nc_type_mask_tests' rustdoc; unkillable by construction.

### The six timeouts

Not survivors, and five of them cannot become fast kills.
`NormalizedIter`'s space-run loop went from a peek-and-next pair to
`Peekable::next_if_eq`: the pair's condition reversed consumes nothing
and never ends, because next() on an exhausted Peekable leaves peek() at
None forever. next_if_eq has no comparison to reverse, so cargo-mutants
no longer generates that mutant at all -- confirmed with --list.

The remaining five replace `next` wholesale or stop the position
advancing, producing an iterator that never returns None. names_match
consumes these to exhaustion, so the suite detects them by not
finishing; a timeout is the only verdict available. Two new direct tests
on the iterators do fail in three to five seconds when run alone, which
is what the coverage question was. Hand-verifying one of these leaves a
runaway test binary -- it happened twice today -- so kill by PID, not
with pkill -f, whose pattern matches the invoking shell as well."}

{"notes":"## The full sweep, and why it mattered

541 mutants, 472 caught, 8 missed, 56 unviable, 5 timeouts, 31 minutes
(-j 3, -E 'tests_|_tests::').

I had closed 18 survivors by hand and reported the crate down to one.
The sweep found eight: the one equivalent mutant I expected, and seven
real ones my hand-verification had missed or misjudged. All seven are now
closed -- e4cbe537, 20fd63e6, 28441573 -- each mutation hand-verified.

### The two I had misjudged

check_san_name_form's unevaluable-name-form guard, which I recorded this
morning as subsumed by check_name_constraints' generic SAN loop. True,
and true only because every fixture put the form in a PERMITTED subtree,
where the refusal is overdetermined: a name the matchers cannot decide
matches no subtree, and a constrained type matching nothing is a
violation, so the generic check refuses it whether or not the guard ran.
An EXCLUDED subtree inverts it -- matching nothing means matching no
exclusion, so the certificate passes and the guard is the only thing
refusing it. Same inversion for check_mailbox_against_rfc822's ASCII
requirement. Both fail open in the direction that widens a CA's trust
scope past what it published.

### The two I had never seen

chain_walk's `if i == 0` on required_leaf_policy_oids and
required_leaf_subject_dn_attrs. Mutated to `i != 0` each requirement
applies to every certificate except the leaf, so a leaf failing it is
accepted whenever an intermediate satisfies it. Invisible because the
only chain testing them is PKITS AllCertificatesSamePoliciesTest10 --
every certificate asserts the same policies, so no verdict it produces
can distinguish the leaf from the rest of the path.

### The policy_graph cluster

apply_policy_mappings' has_any, intersect_user_policy_set's node lookup,
and prune_above_deepest. All three shape the valid_policy_graph rather
than the verdict, and the §6.1.5 walk counts nodes and parents, so a
wrong shape answers the wrong question without failing. Tested against
the graph directly. Reaching the second took three attempts: the policy
must arrive below depth 1 through a mapping, its ancestor must stay in
the user set, and the leaf step needs may_expand_any_policy. That
arrangement is in the test's rustdoc.

### What remains

One missed mutant: NcTypeMask::RFC822's `1 << 0`, where `1 >> 0` is also
1. Equivalent, unkillable, noted in nc_type_mask_tests.

Five timeouts: the DirStringBytes and NormalizedIter next/position
mutants, which produce iterators that never return None. names_match
consumes them to exhaustion, so the suite detects them by not finishing;
a timeout is the only verdict available. Two bounded direct tests fail
in seconds when run alone. The sixth timeout is gone -- Peekable::next_if_eq
removed that comparison from the mutation space, confirmed with --list.

Both lessons generalised into AGENTS.md (995d33e1)."}
